rca.rootCause: SQLFluff's Jinja templater has custom code that attempts to detect undeclared Jinja variables and provide better error handling. This custom undefined-variable check does not account for Jinja 'block assignment' syntax (e.g. `{% set some_var %}1{% endset %}`), which was introduced in Jinja 2.8. When a variable is defined using block assignment inside an `{% if %}` block, SQLFluff's static analysis fails to recognize it as a defined variable and incorrectly reports 'Undefined jinja template variable' for subsequent references to that variable. The fix needs to make the undefined variable detection logic more sophisticated to recognize block-style `{% set %}...{% endset %}` variable declarations.

def test__templater_jinja_dynamic_variable_no_violations():
    """Test that block-style set inside if doesn't raise undefined variable."""
    in_str = (
        "{% if True %}\n"
        "    {% set some_var %}1{% endset %}\n"
        "    SELECT {{some_var}}\n"
        "{% endif %}"
    )
    t = JinjaTemplater(override_context=dict(blah="foo", condition="a < 10"))
    _, violations = t.process(in_str=in_str, fname="test", config=FluffConfig())
    assert not violations
